get.summary: Authorization server metadata (RFC 8414)
Protected resource metadata for the Open API (RFC 9728)
get.description: Tells clients which resource indicator to request and which authorization server issues tokens for /open/v1.

resource.description: Always `<API_BASE>/open/v1`; pass it as `resource` in authorize/token requests.

get.summary: Start the authorization-code flow (PKCE S256 required)
get.description: Validates the request, stores it for 10 minutes and redirects (302) the browser to the LunaTalk login/consent page (the provider's login page with `oauth_request=<id>` (an alternate domain is used when `login_site=pro` or the request host is the `.pro` API). After the user logs in and approves/denies (the consent page uses the internal endpoints `POST /oauth/authorize/context` and `POST /oauth/authorize/complete`, which require a LunaTalk web session and are not part of the client-facing contract), the browser is redirected to `redirect_uri` with `code` and `state` (approve), or `error=access_denied` and `state` (deny), or `error=temporarily_unavailable` if the request expired. The authorization code is valid for 10 minutes and single-use. Validation failures of this endpoint itself are returned as 400 JSON, not as an error redirect.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: From /oauth/register.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Must exactly match one registered redirect URI.

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description: PKCE challenge: base64url(SHA-256(code_verifier)), no padding.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: Resource indicator (RFC 8707). Use `<API_BASE>/open/v1` for the Open API; the token is only valid on that resource.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Only the single scope exists; omit or send exactly this value.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque value echoed back on the redirect.

parameters.name: login_site
parameters.description: Send `pro` to use the alternate login domain (for regions where the main domain is blocked). Any other value is ignored.

302.description: Redirect to the login/consent page. Later the user agent is redirected to `redirect_uri?code=...&state=...` or `redirect_uri?error=access_denied&state=...`.

400.description: `unsupported_response_type`, `invalid_client`, `invalid_redirect_uri`, `unsupported_pkce`, `invalid_scope`, `invalid_resource`.

post.summary: Dynamic client registration (RFC 7591)
post.description: Registers a public client (no secret; `token_endpoint_auth_method` is `none`). `client_name`: 1-80 characters after whitespace normalization, no control/bidi characters. `redirect_uris`: at least one; `https` with a host, `http` only for `localhost`/loopback IPs, or a custom scheme with a host or path (`javascript`, `data`, `file`, `vbscript` are rejected; fragments and userinfo are rejected). `grant_types`: subset of `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`; must include `authorization_code`; defaults to both when omitted.

400.description: `invalid_client_metadata` or `invalid_redirect_uri`.

post.summary: Revoke an access or refresh token (RFC 7009)
post.description: Form-encoded (or multipart) field `token`: an access token or a refresh token (detected by lookup). Revoking either revokes the whole session it belongs to (all access and refresh tokens of that grant); a legacy session-less access token is revoked individually. Returns 200 with an empty body whether or not the token was found.

400.description: `invalid_request` — missing token.

post.summary: Exchange a code or refresh token for tokens
post.description: Accepts `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (or multipart form) fields only — a JSON body is NOT parsed and results in `unsupported_grant_type`. No client authentication (public clients). `authorization_code`: `code`, `client_id`, `redirect_uri` (must equal the one used at authorize), `code_verifier` (PKCE), `resource` (must equal the one used at authorize); the code is single-use and must be presented with exactly the same `client_id`, `redirect_uri` and `resource` as the authorize request and a `code_verifier` whose S256 challenge equals the registered `code_challenge`; any mismatch is `invalid_grant`. `refresh_token`: `refresh_token`, `client_id`, `resource` (must match the session), optional `scope` (must be `mcp:card-writer` if given). Refresh tokens are single-use and rotated: each successful refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token; presenting an already-used refresh token revokes the whole session (all its tokens) and returns `invalid_grant`. Access tokens live 8 hours (`expires_in` 28800); the session/refresh token lives 30 days from the original grant. Clients registered without the `refresh_token` grant, and server-configured long-access fallback clients, receive no `refresh_token` (fallback clients get a 30-day access token, `expires_in` 2592000).

400.description: `unsupported_grant_type`, `invalid_client`, `invalid_grant`.

post.summary: Post a comment or reply
post.description: Creates a top-level comment (no `parentId`/`rootId`) or a reply. The comment's locale is taken from the `language` header (default `zh-Hant`). Content is checked synchronously against a banned-word list: on a hit the comment is still created but immediately hidden/rejected (the response looks identical); otherwise it is visible right away with `reviewStatus=pending` and moderated asynchronously. Requires a bearer.

400.description: `roleId is required`, `content or imageUrls is required`, malformed JSON, or database error text.

get.summary: Number of visible comments on a card
get.description: Guest-readable. Counts visible comments in the caller's locale (plus the caller's own rejected ones when authenticated).

400.description: `roleId is required` or database error text.

401.description: `unauthorized` — only when a bearer is present but invalid.

post.summary: Delete a comment
post.description: Soft-deletes a comment. Allowed for the comment author or the author of the card the comment belongs to (`roleId` is optional; the comment's own card is used as fallback). Reply counts are adjusted.

roleId.description: Optional card id for the creator-permission check.

400.description: `commentId is required`, `comment not found`, `no permission to delete`, `delete failed`, or malformed JSON.

post.summary: Like or unlike a comment

400.description: `invalid parameters` or database error text.

get.summary: Top-level comments of a card
get.description: Guest-readable. Returns visible top-level comments for the card in the caller's `language` locale (zh-Hans and zh-Hant are treated as one locale; other locales match exactly; no `language` header = no locale filter), ordered pinned first, then by like count, then newest. Each comment embeds up to 3 replies. The caller's own rejected comments are included (with `reviewStatus`/`rejectReason`) when authenticated. `sortBy` is accepted but currently ignored.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Ignored by the server.

400.description: `invalid parameters` (missing roleId or page values < 1) or database error text.

401.description: `unauthorized` — only when a bearer is present but invalid.

get.summary: Replies under a top-level comment
get.description: Guest-readable. Paginated replies whose `rootId` is the given comment, same locale/visibility rules as the list endpoint. `roleId` is optional and only used to compute `isCreator`/`canDelete` against the card author.

parameters.name: rootId
parameters.description: Top-level comment id.

400.description: `invalid parameters` or database error text.

401.description: `unauthorized` — only when a bearer is present but invalid.

get.summary: List the saved conversations (archives) of one card
get.description: Returns every non-deleted conversation the caller has with the given role card (the current one plus history), most recently updated first. At most 500 entries are returned in one response (no paging parameter is exposed). `count` is the number of non-deleted conversations for this card and `limit` is the per-card archive cap (20): when `count >= limit`, `POST /conversation/fork` and `POST /conversation/save-and-start-new` answer 409. `messageCount` excludes compaction-summary rows. `lastMessage` is the most recent message, whitespace-collapsed and truncated to 80 characters.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Role card id whose conversations are listed.

400.description: `bad_request` — `roleId` is missing or blank.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — a service-account key (`lsk_...`) cannot call this route.

500.description: `internal` — the archive list could not be loaded (`retryable: true`).

post.summary: Switch a conversation to current, or roll its history back to a message
post.description: Two modes. (1) Without `chatId`: make `conversationId` the CURRENT conversation for its role (the previous CURRENT one becomes HISTORY); response `{"success":"ok"}`. (2) With `chatId` (string chat id, or the numeric row `id` as a JSON number): roll the conversation back so that the given message becomes the tail; later rows are trimmed (branching/superseding rules are internal), the in-flight stream for the superseded branch is stopped, and derived state (prompt ledger, memory, profile) is rolled back. Rollback is a durable, idempotent operation: declare `rollbackMutationCapability:"v1"` and supply a `clientOperationID` to get outcome_v1 semantics (409 on terminal failure, 202 while repair is pending, identical results on replay). Omitting `rollbackMutationCapability` selects the legacy contract: a server-generated operation id, `legacyCompatibility:true`, and — when the canonical timeline already committed but derived cleanup is still pending — HTTP 200 with `status:"repair_pending"` and `repairPending:true` instead of 202. Any other non-empty `rollbackMutationCapability` value is rejected with 409 `rollback_client_unsupported`. Note the response key is `operationID` (capital ID), unlike `operationId` in the operations endpoints.

200.description: Load mode: `{"success":"ok"}`. Rollback mode: `{"success":"ok"}` when the request is a semantic no-op; otherwise `status:"success"` with `operationID`, `supportCode`, `targetRowID` (and `legacyCompatibility:true` on the legacy path). Legacy path only: `status:"repair_pending"` with `repairPending:true`, `canonicalTimelineCommitted:true`, `error`/`errorCode` naming the pending repair.

202.description: Rollback accepted but not finished: `status` `rollback_pending` (an identical in-progress operation is being replayed) or `repair_pending` (timeline committed, derived cleanup fenced and retried in the background). `error`/`errorCode` carry the pending reason; poll `GET /open/v1/conversation/operations`.

400.description: `errorCode` one of `bind_json` (malformed body), `missing_conversation_id`, `missing_operation_id` (capability v1 without `clientOperationID`), `load_conversation_error` (load mode failed; `error` = text), `rollback_target_error` (target could not be resolved; `error` = text).

403.description: `service_account_forbidden`.

409.description: `errorCode` one of `rollback_client_unsupported`, `server_busy` (retryable), `operation_in_progress` (retryable), or a terminal replay of a failed/superseded operation (`rollback_failed`, `rollback_superseded`, or the operation's stored error code) with `status` `failed`/`superseded` and `operationID`/`supportCode`/`targetRowID`.

post.summary: Delete a conversation and all of its messages
post.description: Deletes the conversation row owned by the caller together with its messages, prompt ledger, memory store and pin record. Idempotent: if no conversation matches (unknown id or not owned) nothing is deleted and the response is still `200 {"success":"ok"}`.

400.description: Malformed JSON, `missing conversationId`, or database error (`error` = text).

403.description: `service_account_forbidden`.

post.summary: Delete one message from a conversation
post.description: Deletes the row (`conversationId`, `chatId`) and bumps the conversation history epoch in the same transaction, so any in-flight generation or compaction for the conversation fails closed. Afterwards the prompt ledger is reset (a snapshot restore is attempted when the deleted row was the latest row). Both keys are read with unchecked type assertions: a body where either is missing or not a string results in HTTP 500 with an empty body (panic recovery). The handler does not check that the conversation belongs to the caller; deleting an unknown pair is a no-op returning 200.

400.description: Malformed JSON (`{"error":<text>}`) or database error as a localized `I18nError` with `code` `err.internal.db_error` / `err.business.not_found`.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden`.

409.description: `server_busy` (retryable) — the operation kernel is not active for this conversation.

500.description: Prompt-ledger reset failed (`I18nError`, `code` `err.internal.db_error`), or missing/non-string `conversationId`/`chatId` (panic recovery, empty body).

post.summary: Add a manual standing instruction
post.description: Appends a new user-authored standing instruction to the conversation and returns the updated visible list. `text` is trimmed, must be 1–200 characters and must not contain `<` or `>`. At most 10 visible directives may exist. The change takes effect on the next generation without invalidating the prompt cache. Errors use the legacy `{error}` shape where `error` is the code.

400.description: `error` = `DIRECTIVE_EMPTY` (blank text), `DIRECTIVE_TOO_LONG` (over 200 characters), `DIRECTIVE_INVALID_CHARS` (contains `<` or `>`), `DIRECTIVE_LIMIT_REACHED` (already 10 visible directives), "missing conversationId", "conversation not found", or a JSON binding error message.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

post.summary: Remove a standing instruction
post.description: Retires the directive identified by `sourceId` so it is no longer visible or injected. Returns the updated visible list. `text` is ignored.

400.description: `error` = `DIRECTIVE_NOT_FOUND` (`sourceId` blank or no visible directive with that id), "missing conversationId", "conversation not found", or a JSON binding error message.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

post.summary: Replace the text of a standing instruction
post.description: Replaces the text of the directive identified by `sourceId` (from the list endpoint) and marks it as user-authored (`origin: "manual"`); automatically extracted directives can be edited this way too. Same text rules as add (trimmed, 1–200 characters, no `<`/`>`). Returns the updated visible list.

400.description: `error` = `DIRECTIVE_NOT_FOUND` (`sourceId` blank or no visible directive with that id), `DIRECTIVE_EMPTY`, `DIRECTIVE_TOO_LONG`, `DIRECTIVE_INVALID_CHARS`, "missing conversationId", "conversation not found", or a JSON binding error message.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

get.summary: List the standing instructions of a conversation
get.description: Returns the currently visible standing instructions (long-term user directives) of a conversation the caller owns, one entry per slot, in ledger order. Entries come either from the user (type `manual`) or were extracted automatically from the dialogue (types `language`, `format`, `perspective`, `boundary`). `maxCount` (10) and `maxLength` (200 characters) are the limits enforced by the add/update endpoints. Errors use the legacy `{error}` shape.

parameters.name: conversationId
parameters.description: Conversation whose directives are listed.

400.description: `error` = "missing conversationId" or "conversation not found" (unknown id or not owned by the caller).

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

post.summary: Save a conversation and branch a new current conversation from it
post.description: Keeps the source conversation as history (if it is the current conversation of the card it is demoted, together with any other current conversation of the same card) and creates a new current conversation containing a copy of the source messages. Only message rows are copied (new message ids, same content, roles, order and timestamps); token statistics, memory links, pinned items, queued turns and compaction summaries are not carried over, so context compaction and long-term memory of the new conversation start from scratch. With `chatId` set, only messages up to and including that message are copied ("fork from this message"); the id must belong to the source conversation. A generation that is still streaming into the source conversation is asked to stop. Subject to the per-card archive limit: if the card already has 20 non-deleted conversations the request is rejected with 409 and nothing is changed or auto-deleted.

400.description: `bad_request` — body is not valid JSON or `conversationId` is missing/blank. `title_too_long` — `title` exceeds 100 characters. `chat_not_found` — `chatId` is not a message of the source conversation.

403.description: `forbidden` — the conversation does not exist, is deleted, or is not owned by the caller (message is always "conversation not found"; a database error while resolving the conversation also yields this response). `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

409.description: `conversation_limit_reached` — the card already has `limit` (20) non-deleted conversations. Delete or keep existing archives; nothing is removed automatically.

500.description: `internal` — archives could not be counted or the fork failed (`retryable: true`).

get.summary: List the caller's current conversations
get.description: Pages over the caller's CURRENT conversations that contain at least one user message, ordered by last update descending, joined with role name/greeting/description (localized for `en`/`ja`/`ko` via the `language` header) and the last chat message preview. `pageSize` must be a positive integer: the handler computes `total % pageSize` without a default, so a missing or zero `pageSize` causes a divide-by-zero panic (HTTP 500, empty body).

parameters.name: pageNum
parameters.description: 1-based page. Non-numeric or <1 → 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Items per page. Required in practice: 0/missing → 500.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Selects localized role fields and avatar host. Missing or unrecognized values are normalized to `en` by a global middleware.

400.description: Database error (`error` = error text).

403.description: `service_account_forbidden`.

500.description: `pageSize` missing or 0 (division by zero, panic recovery). Empty body.

get.summary: List the active long-term memory entries of a conversation
get.description: Returns the long-term memory entries (atoms) of a conversation the caller owns. Only entries with `status: "active"` are returned (superseded, decayed and archived entries are filtered out). The response body is a bare JSON array. Errors use the legacy `{error}` shape.

parameters.name: conversationId
parameters.description: Conversation whose memory is listed.

403.description: Legacy `{error: "forbidden"}` — the conversation belongs to another account. Canonical `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

404.description: `error` = "conversation not found" (unknown id; also returned when the ownership lookup fails).

503.description: `error` = "memory service not available" — the memory subsystem is not enabled on this server.

delete.description: Archives the given memory entry of a conversation the caller owns and removes it from retrieval. Only entries that are currently `active` can be deleted; any other status is reported as not found. Errors use the legacy `{error}` shape.

parameters.name: conversationId
parameters.description: Conversation that owns the entry.

parameters.name: atomId
parameters.description: `atomId` from the list endpoint.

403.description: Legacy `{error: "forbidden"}` — the conversation, or the entry itself, belongs to another account. Canonical `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

404.description: `error` = "conversation not found" (unknown conversation or ownership lookup failure) or "atom not found" (no such entry in this conversation, or the entry is not `active`).

get.summary: List messages of a conversation (newest first) or fetch specific messages by id
get.description: Paged history of the caller's conversation, ordered by `createTime` descending (page 1 = newest). Ownership is verified; another account's conversation returns 403. When `chatId` and/or `chatIds` are given, pagination is ignored and only those rows (max 20 ids, oldest first) are returned, with `total` equal to the number of rows found. Queued-but-not-yet-dispatched user turns (`turnStatus:"queued"`) are included. Message text is returned verbatim for v1 clients (no Traditional-Chinese conversion). AI rows get `isV3:true` when the role uses an XMLV3 theme. On page 1 a `contextFootprint` object is added when it can be computed (otherwise the key is absent). With `supportsOperationOutcome=true` the response additionally carries `schemaVersion`, `operations` (recent operation statuses for this conversation, most recent first, up to 50, with stop→continue chains collapsed), `operationStatusAvailable`, and — only when there is at least one — `agentPrepTraces` keyed by operationId. If the operation projection store fails, `operations` is `[]` and `operationStatusAvailable` is `false`; do not treat that as proof that no operation exists (use `GET /open/v1/conversation/operations`).

parameters.name: conversationId
parameters.description: Conversation to read. Empty → 403 (ownership check fails).

parameters.name: pageNum
parameters.description: 1-based page. Non-numeric or <1 → 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Rows per page. Non-numeric or <=0 → 80.

parameters.name: chatId
parameters.description: Fetch a single message by id (may also be a comma-separated list). Switches to by-id mode.

parameters.name: chatIds
parameters.description: Repeatable and/or comma-separated message ids. Combined with `chatId`, de-duplicated, capped at 20.

parameters.name: supportsOperationOutcome
parameters.description: `true` adds `schemaVersion`, `operations`, `operationStatusAvailable` and optional `agentPrepTraces`.

400.description: Database error (`error` = error text).

403.description: `{"error":"forbidden"}` — conversation does not belong to the caller (or `conversationId` empty); or `service_account_forbidden`.

get.summary: Read the player notepad of a conversation
get.description: Returns the free-form notepad text attached to a conversation the caller owns. An empty `content` is returned when no notepad has been saved. `maxLength` (10000 characters) is the save limit; notepads longer than `discountThreshold` (2000 characters) forfeit the reduced-price prompt-cache accounting on each turn. Errors use the legacy `{error}` shape.

parameters.name: conversationId
parameters.description: Conversation whose notepad is read.

400.description: `error` = "missing conversationId" or "conversation not found" (unknown id or not owned by the caller).

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

post.summary: Replace the player notepad of a conversation
post.description: Overwrites the notepad text of a conversation the caller owns (full replacement; an empty string clears it). The write is a pure data update: it does not create a message, trigger a reply, consume credits or affect the prompt cache. Content is limited to 10000 characters. Concurrent saves for the same conversation are serialized; last write wins.

400.description: `{error: "NOTEPAD_TOO_LONG", errorCode: "NOTEPAD_TOO_LONG", maxLength: 10000}` when `content` exceeds the limit; otherwise `{error}` with "missing conversationId", "conversation not found", or a JSON binding error message.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

get.summary: List chat operation statuses of a conversation
get.description: Account-owned read model of chat operations (send, regenerate, continue, backward) for one conversation, most recently updated first, cursor-paged. Stop→continue chains of Agent-mode turns are collapsed into one entry. Use it to reconcile a turn after a disconnect: `state` tells whether a reply was persisted (`assistantChatId`), and `allowedActions` what the client may offer next. `operationStatusAvailable:false` means the durable projection is not active for this conversation (statuses are not authoritative).

parameters.name: conversationId
parameters.description: Conversation owned by the caller.

parameters.name: clientOperationId
parameters.description: Filter to the operation created with this client operation id.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size; values above 50 are clamped to 50. Non-numeric or <=0 → 400 `invalid_limit`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque `nextCursor` from a previous page. Malformed → 400 `invalid_cursor`.

400.description: `errorCode` one of `conversation_id_required`, `invalid_limit`, `invalid_cursor` (`status:"failed"`).

403.description: `service_account_forbidden`.

404.description: `operation_not_found` (`status:"not_found"`) — the conversation does not exist for this account.

get.summary: Get one chat operation status
get.description: Returns the status projection of a single operation owned by the caller. Operation ids come from `operationStatus` WebSocket events, `GET /open/v1/conversation/operations`, or the `operations[]` block of `GET /open/v1/conversation/messages`.

parameters.name: operationId
parameters.description: Server operation id.

400.description: `operation_id_required` (blank path segment).

403.description: `service_account_forbidden`.

404.description: `operation_not_found` (`status:"not_found"`) — unknown or not owned; or `operation_status_unavailable` (`status:"unavailable"`) — exists but the durable projection is not active.

get.summary: Context-usage breakdown of the latest turn of a conversation
get.description: Returns how the prompt of the most recent AI turn was composed (per-component character/token estimates and percentages), cache statistics, billing points and worldbook recall results. `status` is `ok` when a snapshot exists, `notReady` when the model supports diagnostics but no turn has been recorded yet, `unsupportedModel` when the conversation's model does not use the cache-stable context pipeline. `breakdownVersion=2` splits `mod`, `notepad` and `directive` out of `system` (11 items instead of 8) and sets `schemaVersion:2`. Worldbook entry names in `worldbookRecall.entries[]` are returned only to the role's author; other callers receive entries with `name` omitted.

parameters.name: conversationId
parameters.description: Conversation owned by the caller.

parameters.name: breakdownVersion
parameters.description: `2` selects the 11-item breakdown; any other value means 1.

400.description: `missing conversationId`.

403.description: `{"error":"conversation not found"}` — not owned or unknown; or `service_account_forbidden`.

get.summary: Fetch the persisted text of one AI message
get.description: Returns the stored body of the AI message `chatId` (AI rows only; pending compaction summaries are excluded). Intended for reading back a reply after a stream ended or was interrupted. When no matching AI row exists the response is still 200 with `message` empty and `isComplete:false`. The lookup is by `chatId` alone; the handler does not take a conversation parameter. Text is returned verbatim (no script-conversion for v1).

parameters.name: chatId
parameters.description: Chat message identifier (the `chatId` field of a message, a UUID string).

400.description: Database error (`error` = error text).

403.description: `service_account_forbidden`.

post.summary: Manually replace the text of the latest AI message in a conversation
post.description: Manual edit, not regeneration: overwrites the body of the latest canonical AI row of the conversation with `content` and clears its stored thinking. The target must be the latest non-summary, non-queued row; if a later USER or AI row exists the edit is rejected. The edit advances the conversation history epoch so any in-flight generation for the conversation fails closed. Identical concurrent requests are coalesced. Note the request key is spelled `conversionId` (verbatim). An empty `conversionId` returns 200 without doing anything. To regenerate an AI reply with the model, use the WebSocket with `rewrite:true` instead (see `POST /open/v1/conversation/ws-ticket`).

200.description: Edit applied (or no-op when `conversionId` is empty).

400.description: `invalid request body` (malformed JSON or `conversionId`/`content` not strings) as `{"error":"invalid request body"}`; or `errorCode` `rewrite_target_invalid` — target missing, not an editable AI row, or not owned by the caller (these cases are deliberately indistinguishable).

403.description: `service_account_forbidden`.

409.description: `errorCode` one of `rewrite_target_not_latest` (a newer row exists; refresh), `operation_in_progress` (retryable), `server_busy` (retryable).

post.summary: Manually replace the text of an AI message identified by chatId
post.description: Same manual-edit semantics as `/open/v1/conversation/rewrite`, but the target is selected by `chatId`. The row must be the latest canonical AI row of a conversation owned by the caller; otherwise `rewrite_target_invalid` / `rewrite_target_not_latest`. `chatId` must be the string chat identifier (a numeric value is rejected with 400). An empty `chatId` returns 200 without doing anything.

200.description: Edit applied (or no-op when `chatId` is empty).

400.description: `{"error":"invalid request body"}` for malformed input, or `errorCode` `rewrite_target_invalid`.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden`.

post.summary: Archive the given conversation and start a fresh one for the same card
post.description: Ends the given conversation and creates a new current conversation for the same role card, seeded with the card's welcome message. Whether the old conversation is kept as history or discarded is decided by the server: if it contains at least one user message it is kept as history, otherwise it is marked deleted. The `save` field is required but only labels the request in server metrics; it does not change that decision. If the old conversation is no longer current (for example a concurrent duplicate request already archived it) the existing current conversation of the card is returned instead of creating another one. A generation still streaming into the old conversation is asked to stop. Subject to the per-card archive limit: if the card already has 20 non-deleted conversations the request is rejected with 409 before anything changes. Role fields in `roleInfo` and the welcome text are returned verbatim (no per-language conversion on this API); the optional `language` header only chooses the generic fallback player name substituted into `defaultRelay` when neither a persona name, the card's player name nor the account nickname is available.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Only used to pick the language of the generic fallback player name substituted into `defaultRelay`. Defaults to `zh-Hans` when absent.

parameters.name: X-XMLV3-Feature-Level
parameters.description: XML v3 renderer feature level supported by the client; reported back in `xmlV3Compatibility.clientFeatureLevel`. Defaults to 1.

200.description: The new current conversation and its opening message.

400.description: Canonical `bad_request` (body unreadable/not JSON or `conversationId` missing/blank), or a legacy `{error: <free text>}` from the underlying start-new step (conversation lookup, role lookup or welcome-message insert failed).

403.description: `forbidden` — the conversation does not exist, is deleted, or is not owned by the caller (message "conversation not found"). `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

409.description: `conversation_limit_reached` — the card already has `limit` (20) non-deleted conversations; no new conversation is created and the old one is untouched.

500.description: `internal` — archives could not be counted (`retryable: true`). An empty-body 500 is returned when `save` is missing or not a boolean.

post.summary: Open (or resume) the current conversation with a role
post.description: Synchronous. Returns the CURRENT conversation for the pair (caller account, `roleId`), creating one atomically if none exists. On a newly created conversation the role's greeting is inserted as the first AI message (`isFirst:true`); `greetingIndex` selects an alternate greeting for that first message. On an existing conversation nothing is inserted (`historyConversation:true`). This endpoint does not generate a reply and does not stream: sending a message, regenerating or continuing happens over the WebSocket documented on `POST /open/v1/conversation/ws-ticket` (`x-websocket`). Side effects: bumps the role's talk counter and daily-task progress. `roleInfo` is localized according to the `language` header and has `roleDetailDesc`/`roleDetailDescEn`/`roleDetailDescJa`/`roleDetailDescKo` blanked; `roleWelcome` and `defaultRelay` have `{{char}}`/`{{user}}` placeholders substituted. Avatar/background hosts are rewritten per language. The optional `X-XMLV3-Feature-Level` header (positive integer, default 1) declares the client's XMLV3 renderer level and is echoed in `xmlV3Compatibility`. Note: the handler reads `roleId` with an unchecked type assertion; a body without a string `roleId` results in HTTP 500 with an empty body (panic recovery), not 400.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Localizes `roleInfo` and the greeting. A global middleware normalizes this header and substitutes `en` when it is missing or unrecognized.

parameters.name: X-XMLV3-Feature-Level
parameters.description: Client XMLV3 renderer feature level (latest is 4). Used to compute `xmlV3Compatibility`.

400.description: Malformed JSON body, unknown role, or conversation creation failure. `error` is a free-text message, not a code.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call conversation routes.

500.description: Body had no string `roleId` (unchecked type assertion → panic recovery). Empty body.

post.summary: Stop the reply currently being generated for a conversation
post.description: Requests cancellation of the in-flight generation for `conversationId`. With `streamId` (from the WebSocket `streamMeta` event) the exact stream session is targeted; without it, the active session for the conversation is used. Also marks any durable pending operation for the conversation as stopped. The response is `200 {"message":"success"}` whether or not a stream was actually running (no active stream, unknown streamId, stream/conversation mismatch and already-finished streams all return 200). Equivalent to sending the `{"action":"stop"}` control frame on the WebSocket. The partial reply already streamed is kept and persisted.

400.description: Malformed JSON body (`error` = parser text) or `conversationId is required`.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden`.

503.description: `stop request could not be recorded` — the stop could not be persisted; retry.

post.summary: Generate a suggested next player message
post.description: Writes one candidate message in the player's voice (1–3 sentences, same language as the conversation, at most 600 characters) from the role summary and the last 12 messages. The text is returned for the client to place in the input box; it is not sent. Costs 10 points per generation, charged only on success. The generated text is cached for 24 h keyed on the latest message of the conversation: repeated calls return the cached text with `cost:0` and `cached:true` until the conversation advances; pass `regenerate:true` to force a new (charged) generation. Concurrent identical requests are coalesced into one generation. Ownership: a conversation not owned by the caller is reported as 403 `forbidden`.

400.description: `bad_request` — malformed body or empty `conversationId`.

402.description: `insufficient_credits` — not enough points; body also carries `cost` (10).

403.description: `forbidden` — conversation not found or not owned; or `service_account_forbidden`.

502.description: `internal` (retryable) — upstream model failed or returned nothing; no points charged.

post.summary: Make a saved conversation the current conversation of its card
post.description: Switches the given conversation to be the card's current conversation; the previously current conversation of the same card becomes history. Nothing is deleted. Internally this runs the branch-switch path at the conversation's latest message, which also fences in-flight generation on the old current conversation (streams are stopped, pending operations are invalidated). If the conversation has no messages a plain tag swap is performed. Any 2xx outcome of the underlying switch (including a deferred-cleanup outcome) is reported as 200 with the archive-oriented body below; non-2xx outcomes are passed through unchanged in the legacy error shape.

400.description: Either the canonical `bad_request` (body not valid JSON or `conversationId` missing/blank, `{error, message, retryable}`), or a passthrough legacy error from the switch itself: `{error: <free text>, errorCode}` with `errorCode` = `load_conversation_error` (tag swap failed) or `rollback_target_error` (branch switch could not resolve its target).

403.description: `forbidden` — the conversation does not exist, is deleted, or is not owned by the caller (message "conversation not found"). `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

409.description: Passthrough from the switch: `operation_in_progress` (another history mutation on this conversation is still pending) or `server_busy` (the operation kernel is not active). Both carry `retryable: true`; retry after a short delay.

500.description: Passthrough from the switch: `errorCode` = `rollback_operation_missing`, `rollback_outcome_invalid`, `rollback_repair_state_failed` or `rollback_complete_failed` (the last two carry `status: "repair_pending"`, `operationID` and `supportCode`; the branch switch itself has been committed and derived cleanup is retried server-side). Other terminal-replay projections of the switch may emit additional 500 codes.

post.summary: Set or clear the title of a conversation
post.description: Sets the user-visible title of a conversation the caller owns. `title` must be present: a non-empty string (at most 100 characters) sets the title, an empty string clears it. Responses use the legacy `{error}` shape without `message`/`retryable`.

400.description: `invalid_request` — body is not valid JSON or `title` is absent/null. `invalid_conversation_id` — `conversationId` missing or blank. `title_too_long` — more than 100 characters.

403.description: `forbidden` — the conversation is not owned by the caller (legacy shape `{error: "forbidden"}`). `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route (canonical shape).

500.description: `conversation_title_update_failed` — the update could not be stored.

post.summary: Issue a one-time ticket for the chat WebSocket
post.description: Browsers cannot send `Authorization` on a WebSocket upgrade, so streaming identity is proven with a short-lived ticket: call this endpoint with the bearer token, then open `GET /open/v1/conversation/ws` and send `{"type":"auth","ticket":"<ticket>"}` as the first frame. Tickets are random 256-bit values, valid for 30 seconds, single-use (consumed atomically on first presentation). Only user tokens (OAuth or account token) may obtain tickets. The full WebSocket contract is described in the `x-websocket` extension of this operation. No request body.

401.description: `unauthorized` — missing/invalid bearer (middleware, with `message`), or the identity was not established from a token (handler: `{"error":"unauthorized","retryable":false}`, no `message` key).

403.description: `service_account_forbidden`.

503.description: `internal` (retryable) — ticket store unavailable. Body is `{"error":"internal","retryable":true}` (no `message` key).

x-websocket.description:
Streaming chat endpoint consuming the ticket. The route is registered outside the bearer middleware: send no `Authorization` header; identity comes exclusively from the ticket frame and the `accountId` field of chat frames is ignored. All server frames are WebSocket text frames whose content is SSE-formatted text (`event: <type>
data: <payload>

`, prefixed with `id: <n>
` when `protocolVersion` is 2 or 3), except the raw JSON frames noted below. Third-party clients should always send `protocolVersion=3`: without it the legacy frame format is used (no `id:` lines, no `streamMeta`/`accepted`/`done`/`queued`/`turn_already_consumed`/`sessionExpired` events, no resume). Send `X-Client-Platform: web` on the upgrade request: this route is outside the v1 middleware, so the `web` default applied to HTTP routes is not applied here and the absent-header behavior (content-visibility filtering) is not verified.

protocolVersion.description: Enables id-prefixed frames and the streamMeta/accepted/done/resume protocol. Recommended: `3`. Ticket auth is required on this route regardless.

resumeStreamId.description: Resume mode A: replay/tail an existing stream by the `streamId` received in `streamMeta`. Ownership is checked against the ticket's account.

lastEventId.description: With `resumeStreamId`: last event id already received; events after it are replayed then live-tailed. `0`/absent on an already-finished stream returns only `done` (history is authoritative).

mode.description: Resume mode B: with `conversationId`, attach to the active stream of that conversation (after a page refresh without a stored streamId).

language.description: With `mode=tryResume`: language for the `resumeUnavailable` message (falls back to the `language` header).

clientFirstFrame.description: Must arrive within 10 seconds of the upgrade.

onFailure.description: Unknown, expired or reused ticket, wrong first frame, or timeout; the server then closes the connection.

newStreamFlow: 1. Send the auth frame; wait for `ready`.
2. Send exactly one chat frame (JSON object, see `clientChatFrame`) within 15 seconds.
3. Receive `streamMeta` (protocolVersion 2/3) carrying `streamId`; store it for resume.

4. Receive `accepted` (`chatId` of the persisted user turn), `messageMeta`, optional `prepStep`/`thinking` events, then `answer` deltas, a final `answer` chunk with `finish_reason`, the literal `answer` `[DONE]`, `flowResponses`, optional compaction events, then `done`.
5. Persisted results are readable afterwards via `GET /open/v1/conversation/messages` and `GET /open/v1/conversation/replay`; operation state via `GET /open/v1/conversation/operations`.

6. To cancel, send `{"action":"stop"}` on the same socket (or call `POST /open/v1/conversation/stop`). A second chat payload on the same socket is rejected with `turn_already_consumed` followed by `sessionExpired` and a close.

conversationId.description: Target conversation (from `/conversation/start`). Missing or non-string → raw JSON frame `{"error":"invalid request body"}` and close.

message.description: User message text. Empty for `rewrite`/`contine` turns.

model.description: Model value from `GET /open/v1/models`. Empty → the server default model.

language.description: The value itself is not used for the turn language: when the key is present the account's configured language is used, when absent zh-Hans is used.

from.description: Client origin label; overrides the `from` header for this turn.

storyId.description: Optional story identifier for story-mode roles.

rewrite.description: `true` = regenerate: discard the latest AI reply and generate a new one. `chatId` may name the target row (must match the persisted latest AI/USER tail, otherwise `rewrite_target_not_persisted`).

contine.description: `true` = continue the latest AI reply (verbatim key spelling).

chatId.description: Rewrite/continue target chat id. Empty means "the latest".

thinkingDepth.description: Overrides the saved thinking depth for this turn. Accepted values depend on the model (e.g. `disabled`, `enabled`, `auto`, `adaptive`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `deep`, `max`); see `GET /open/v1/models` `thinkingDepthOptions`.

presetCmd.description: Preset instruction appended to the turn.

agentMode.description: Per-turn override of the saved Agent-mode (multi-pass preparation) preference; omit to use the preference.

supportsInputQueue.description: Declares input-queue capability (queue a plain send while a turn is streaming instead of superseding it). Server-side feature flag; when inactive this has no effect.

clientTurnId.description: Client idempotency key for a queued turn (with `supportsInputQueue`).

supportsPassBlock.description: Opt in to the `passBlock` typed event (multi-pass structured block).

supportsOperationOutcome.description: Opt in to outcome_v1: `operationStatus` events and durable operation semantics.

operationKind.description: Explicit operation kind (authoritative only with `supportsOperationOutcome`); must not conflict with `rewrite`/`contine`.

resumeFromOperationId.description: Agent mode: continue an interrupted operation whose status has `reasonCode` `agent_progress_preserved`. Invalid values are ignored (fresh run).

supportsModExpiryAck.description: Opt in to the MOD-expiry confirmation protocol (`error_type` `mod_expiry_ack_required` with `ackToken`/`expiredMods`).

ackToken.description: Token from a previous `mod_expiry_ack_required` error, resent with the identical message/clientTurnId to proceed.

clientControlFrame.description: `{"action":"stop"}` requests cancellation of the running generation (also valid on a resumed connection). Non-JSON frames and unknown actions are ignored. Application-level pings are not needed: the server sends WebSocket ping control frames and expects pong.

serverFrames.framing:
Text frame containing `id: <n>
` (protocolVersion 2/3 only, resumable events) + `event: <type>
data: <payload>

`. `answer`/`thinking` payloads are OpenAI-style chat-completion chunks; other payloads are JSON objects unless noted.

streamMeta.description: First event of a new stream (protocolVersion 2/3). Use `streamId` for `resumeStreamId` and `POST /conversation/stop`.

accepted.description: User turn persisted; `chatId` is the user row id (protocolVersion 2/3).

queued.description: Input-queue ack: the send was queued behind a running turn (only when the feature is active).

messageMeta.description: Precedes generated deltas; `isV3` tells which renderer to use.

prepStep.description: Agent-mode preparation progress and upstream retry notices. Stage semantics only; the client supplies copy.

answer.data: OpenAI chunk: {id:'',object:'',created:0,model:'',choices:[{delta:{role:'assistant',content},index:0,finish_reason:null}]} for deltas; a final chunk with empty content and `finish_reason` set (e.g. stop, length, content_filter); then the literal string `[DONE]`.
answer.description: Visible reply text. Text is verbatim for v1 (no script conversion).

flowResponses.description: Legacy trailer with constant placeholder values.

passBlock.description: Multi-pass structured block (only with `supportsPassBlock`). Same shape as `passBlocks[]` in `/conversation/replay`.

compactDone.description: Compaction finished; a summary row was written.

done.description: Stream finished (protocolVersion 2/3). Also the only event sent on a cold resume of an already-finished stream.

error.description: Turn failed or was rejected. Written without an `id:` line. Observed `error_type` values (non-exhaustive): connection_error, server_error, server_busy, timeout, rate_limit, empty_response, insufficient_credits, quota_exhausted, model_refused, content_filter, mutation_in_progress, continue_target_invalid, rewrite_target_not_persisted, rewrite_target_lookup_failed, mod_expiry_ack_required. The handshake failure uses `{code:'unauthorized',retryable:false}` instead.

turn_already_consumed.description: A second chat payload was sent on a socket whose turn is already consumed; followed by `sessionExpired` and close.

sessionExpired.description: Resume rejected (unknown/superseded stream, owner mismatch) or socket closing after a rejected payload.

noActiveStream.description: `mode=tryResume`: no active stream and no AI reply in the last 30 s; the client may resend.

hasRecentReply.description: `mode=tryResume`: no active stream but an AI reply completed within 30 s; reload history instead of resending.

resumeUnavailable.description: `mode=tryResume` could not be evaluated (lookup failure or conversation not owned).

cg_update.description: XMLV3 theme roles only: async image placeholder update. Sent as a raw JSON text frame (not SSE-formatted).

state_update.description: Referenced by the replay filter as a V3 typed event; no producer was found in the server source for this build.

post.summary: Delete library items
post.description: Deletes the given items (ids not owned by the caller are ignored). All-or-nothing: if any item is still referenced by a card (avatar/background/preview page) nothing is deleted and 400 `image_in_use` lists the offending URLs. Success body `{code:0,data:{deleted:n}}`.

imageIds.description: Item ids from the list endpoint.

400.description: `invalid_param` (empty list / bad JSON) or `image_in_use` with `imageUrls`.

post.summary: Add items to a folder
post.description: Binds items to the folder. Ids not owned by the caller are silently ignored.

400.description: `invalid_param`.

post.summary: Create a folder
post.description: Creates a folder. Name is checked against the banned-word list and must be unique (normalized) per account; max 50 folders. Success body `{code:0,data:{folderId,name,sortOrder,createTime}}`.

400.description: `invalid_param`, `banned_word`, `duplicate_name`, `folder_limit`.

post.summary: Delete a folder
post.description: Deletes the folder and its item bindings; the media items themselves are kept.

400.description: `invalid_param`.

get.summary: List folders
get.description: All folders of the caller with item counts. Success body `{code:0,data:{folders:[...]}}`.

post.summary: Remove items from a folder

400.description: `invalid_param`.

post.summary: Rename a folder

400.description: `invalid_param`, `banned_word`, `duplicate_name`.

get.summary: List library items
get.description: Paginated list of the caller's media items in one scope, plus quota figures. Side effect: stale generation tasks are expired and images stuck in `pending` moderation for more than 10 minutes are released to `pass`. Success body is `{code:0,data:{...}}`.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `role` requires `roleId`; `folder` requires `folderId`; `unfiled` = items in no folder.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Required when `scope=role`.

parameters.name: folderId
parameters.description: Required when `scope=folder`.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Media kind filter. Absent = images only; `all` = no filter.

parameters.name: pageNum
parameters.description: 1-based page; <1 becomes 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: <1 or >100 becomes 50.

400.description: `invalid_param` — unknown scope/kind or missing roleId/folderId for the scope.

post.summary: Upload a media file to the caller's library
post.description: Multipart upload of one file. The type is detected from the file bytes (client Content-Type is ignored). Images are stored as `moderationState=pending` and moderated asynchronously (rejected images are deleted from the library later); video/audio/font are stored as `unreviewed`. Limits: 100 MiB per file (checked on Content-Length and on the part), 10000 items per account, 500 MiB total per account (only counting files uploaded since byte accounting existed). `roleId` is silently dropped when the card does not exist or is someone else's private card; `folderIds` bindings are best-effort. Success body is the legacy wrapper `{code:0,data:{...}}`.

file.description: The file. Accepted sniffed types: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp (incl. animated), image/gif, video/mp4, video/webm, audio/mpeg (ID3 or raw MPEG frame sync), audio/wave, application/ogg, font/woff2, font/woff, font/ttf, font/otf. Max 104857600 bytes.

roleId.description: Optional card to attribute the file to (own card or any public card).

folderIds.description: Optional; repeat the field for each folder id to bind the new item to.

400.description: `invalid_param` (no `file` part / unreadable; also returned instead of 413 when a chunked/untruthful-Content-Length body exceeds 100 MiB while the multipart form is being read), `invalid_file_type` (unsupported bytes or undecodable image), `quota_image_exceeded`, `quota_bytes_exceeded`.

413.description: `file_too_large` — request or file larger than 100 MiB.

get.summary: Who am I
get.description: Returns the caller's public identity. Third-party clients compare `accountNumId` with the `accountNumId` returned by role detail to know whether the caller authored a card. Accepts user tokens and service-account keys (`accountType` tells which).

404.description: `not_found` — the account behind the token no longer exists.

get.summary: Points ledger
get.description: Paginated list of the caller's points transactions, newest first, optionally filtered by a time window. Legacy handler: errors are `{"error": "<db error text>"}` with 400.

parameters.name: pageNum
parameters.description: 1-based page. Non-numeric or <1 becomes 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Page size. Non-numeric or <1 becomes 10. No upper clamp is enforced.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Time window relative to now in the caller's timezone. Any other value (or absent) means no time filter. `custom` uses `startTime`/`endTime`.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, inclusive lower bound. Only honored with `period=custom`.

parameters.name: endTime
parameters.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, inclusive upper bound. Only honored with `period=custom`.

parameters.name: timezoneOffset
parameters.description: JavaScript-style offset in minutes (UTC minus local, e.g. -480 for UTC+8). Invalid values become 0.

400.description: Database error; body `{"error": "<text>"}`.

get.summary: Points balance and membership plans
get.description: Returns the caller's permanent points, temporary (time-limited) points and the list of currently held membership plans. Top-up is not available through the Open API; send the user to the main site. Service keys are rejected by the middleware (not on the allow-list).

get.summary: Model catalog
get.description: Returns the full model catalog as an ARRAY of groups; each group contains families, each family contains its variants (lanes/channels) sorted by `costScore` ascending. A featured group (global roleplay weekly ranking) may be prepended as the first element. Group names, descriptions and channel labels are localized by the `language` header. Health `status`, uptime summary, dynamic-price estimates, discounts and unlimited-plan coverage are computed at request time. Most variant fields are omitted when zero/empty.

parameters.name: scene
parameters.description: `story` replaces `costScore` with the story-mode price. Any other value is ignored (no error).

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Card id; used to read whether agent mode is on for the card (affects `billingType`, `noLimitEligible`, `noLimitCovered`) and to pick per-card price samples.

parameters.name: contextLevel
parameters.description: Context tier the client intends to use (a `contextBudgetOptions[].value`); affects `noLimitCovered` and dynamic price estimates. Invalid/<=0 becomes 1.

get.summary: Hourly availability history of one model lane
get.description: Hour-by-hour availability buckets for one catalog model value, ending at the current (partial) UTC hour. Always returns exactly `hours` buckets, including empty ones (`total=0`, `state=no_data`). Free-tier models are resolved to their backing lane internally; the returned `model` echoes the requested value.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: A `value` from the /models catalog (case-insensitive match). Unknown values are 404.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Number of hourly buckets. Non-positive or non-integer -> 400. Values above 168 are silently clamped to 168.

400.description: `model parameter is required` or `hours must be a positive integer`.

get.summary: Read one notepad template including its content
get.description: Returns a template owned by the caller, including `content`.

parameters.name: templateId
parameters.description: Template id.

400.description: `error` = "missing templateId" or "template not found" (unknown id or not owned by the caller).

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

post.summary: Delete a notepad template
post.description: Deletes a template owned by the caller. The operation is idempotent: an unknown or already-deleted id still returns 200. Share codes previously issued for the template are not affected (they hold a frozen snapshot).

templateId.description: The id passed in the request.

400.description: `error` = "missing templateId" or a JSON binding error message.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

post.summary: Create or update a notepad template
post.description: With `templateId` set, updates that template (it must be owned by the caller); without it, creates a new template with a server-generated id. `title` is trimmed and must be 1–40 characters; `content` may be empty and is limited to 10000 characters. Creation is refused once the caller owns 50 templates. Editing a template never affects notepads that were filled from it, and does not change share codes already issued for it.

400.description: `errorCode` = `TEMPLATE_TITLE_INVALID` (blank or over 40 characters; includes `maxTitle`), `TEMPLATE_TOO_LONG` (content over 10000 characters; includes `maxLength`), `TEMPLATE_LIMIT_REACHED` (creating a 51st template; includes `maxCount`) — in each case `error` carries the same code. Otherwise `{error}` with "template not found" or a JSON binding error message.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

post.summary: Issue a share code for a notepad template
post.description: Creates a new share code for a template owned by the caller. The template's title and content are frozen into the code at creation time; later edits to the template do not change what the code delivers. Each call issues a new code. Codes have the form `LT-NB-XXXXXXXXX` (type `NB` = notepad template; 8 data characters plus 1 check character from the Crockford base-32 alphabet).

400.description: `error` = "missing templateId" (also for an unparsable body) or "template not found" (unknown id or not owned by the caller).

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

500.description: `error` = "database unavailable" or "code generation failed" (five consecutive collisions on the unique code index).

post.summary: Revoke a share code
post.description: Marks a share code issued by the caller as revoked so it can no longer be previewed or imported. Templates that other users already imported from the code are their own copies and are not affected. `code` accepts the same lenient input as import (case-insensitive, hyphens optional, or the full share link).

200.description: Code revoked (also when it was already revoked).

400.description: `error` = "invalid code" (malformed or bad check character), "code not found" (no such code, or not issued by the caller), or a JSON binding error message.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

get.summary: List the share codes the caller has issued
get.description: Returns all notepad-template share codes issued by the caller, including revoked ones.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

get.summary: List the caller's notepad templates
get.description: Returns the caller's personal notepad templates without their `content` (use the single-template endpoint to read it). `maxCount` (50 templates per account), `maxLength` (10000 content characters) and `maxTitle` (40 title characters) are the limits enforced on save and import.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys cannot call this route.

get.summary: Agent mode (multi-pass) switch for a card

Validation: `systemPrompt` <= 2000 characters; `userName` <= 20; `userDefine` <= 1000; `jailbreak` <= 1500 characters (500 for zh-Hans/zh-Hant `language`) and is trimmed; `personaMode` must be one of the enum values. Moderation: `userName`+`userDefine` are moderated together when either changes; a non-empty changed `jailbreak` is moderated. No server-side enum validation exists for `selectModel`, `context`, `thinkingDepth`, `sandboxLevel`, `limitLevel`, `promptStrategy`, `templateStyle` or `roleSpeech` — send values taken from /models. personaMode derivation when absent: if any of `userName`/`userSex`/`userDefine` is present the mode is set to `custom`; if none is present the mode is left unchanged.

400.description: Malformed JSON, length/enum validation (localized or fixed text), moderation rejection, or database error. Body `{"error": "<text>"}`.

post.summary: Create a private role card
post.description: Creates a new role card owned by the bearer account with `roleVisibility=private` and `reviewStatus=not_submitted`. Only `roleName` is required; content fields are filled afterwards with `POST /role/{roleId}/document` and `PATCH /role/{roleId}/welcome`. `language` is normalized (`en`, `zh-Hant`, `zh-Hans`, `ja`, `ko`, `all`; common aliases such as `zh-TW`, `zh-CN`, `jp`, `kr` are accepted); when omitted the account's language is used, falling back to `zh-Hans`. The card language decides the per-field character limits enforced later (see `GET /role/validate`). `cardType` defaults to `story` and is stored as the card's `roleType`. `contentRatingIntent=r18` marks the card `isR18=true`; any other value leaves it false. `origin` is a self-declared creation source: only whitelisted values (currently `hearthroom`) are stored as the card's `creationMethod`; anything else falls back to `open_api`. The card is stored with platform scope `from=all`. `idempotencyKey` is accepted but not consumed by the create path (no deduplication is performed).

get.description: Returns the editing state of the display-layer asset (regex display rules, mount trigger/layer, page mode, review status, version) for a role owned by the bearer. parameters.name: roleId

403.description: `forbidden` — not the role owner.

get.summary: Read the display rules of a role for rendering
get.description: Player-side read of a role's display rules, used by clients to render the chat. Any bearer-authenticated caller may read it for any existing role (no visibility check, matching the role-detail gate). On the `/open/v1` prefix this route is not in the guest allow-list, so a bearer token is required. Only assets with `status: passed` are served; when the asset is missing or not passed, the empty shape (`rules: []`, `status: none`, `version: 0`, `pageMode: classic`) is returned. `rejectReason` is never included on this route.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Role id.

400.description: `invalid_param` — `roleId` missing.

get.summary: Get a role card by id
get.description: Returns the full role card record for `roleId`. Guest-readable: no Authorization header is required; when a bearer token is present it is used to compute viewer-relative fields (`isFollow`, `isUserFollow`, `hasConversation`) and to decide owner-only fields. There is no visibility check on this route — any caller who knows the roleId (private, waitReview or public) receives the card. Owner-only fields: `roleDetailDesc` and `roleOutputContract` are returned as empty strings to anyone who is not the author (localized variants `roleDetailDescEn/Ja/Ko` and `talkExample` are not blanked by this route). `jailbreak` and `accountId` are always removed by the response scrubber. On this v1 route the server does not apply language conversion to `roleName`/`roleDesc`/`roleWelcome` (author text is returned verbatim); only the avatar/background asset host is rewritten according to the `language` header. `roleTag` and `talkExample` are parsed into arrays here (unlike `/role/mine`). Admin viewers may receive additional moderation keys (not documented). The optional request header `X-XMLV3-Feature-Level` (positive integer, default 1) declares the client's renderer feature level and drives `xmlV3Compatibility`.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Role id (`characterRoleId`). A missing or unknown id yields 400 with `record not found`.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Viewer language. Selects the asset host used in `roleAvatar`/`roleBackground` and the locale used for `commentNum`.

parameters.name: X-XMLV3-Feature-Level
parameters.description: Client XMLV3 renderer feature level; reflected in `xmlV3Compatibility.clientFeatureLevel`.

400.description: `record not found` (unknown roleId) or a database error string. Body is `{"error": "<raw error string>"}` (no `message`/`retryable`).

401.description: `unauthorized` — an Authorization header was sent but the bearer is invalid (guest access only applies when the header is absent).

403.description: `service_account_forbidden` — service-account keys (`lsk_...`) cannot call this route.

get.summary: List the caller's own role cards
get.description: Lists role cards owned by the bearer account, newest `lastUpdateTime` first. Only the caller's cards are ever returned; identity comes from the bearer, not from any parameter. Trial cards (created through `/trial-cards`) are excluded. Cards are filtered by the platform scope `from` header (default `app`): rows whose `from` is the header value or `all` are listed (cards created through this API are stored with `from=all`, so they always appear). Note: `roleDetailDesc`, `roleDetailDescEn`, `roleDetailDescJa` and `roleDetailDescKo` are always returned as empty strings on this route (the owner comparison is made against a cleared value); fetch the definition with `GET /role/detail` using the bearer. `roleTag` and `talkExample` are raw JSON strings in list items (not parsed). Text localization is applied to list items according to the `language` header (default `zh-Hans`): for `zh-Hant` the name/desc/welcome are converted to Traditional Chinese; for cards whose `language` is `all` the en/ja/ko localized variants are substituted when the viewer language is en/ja/ko. `pageSize` must be a positive integer — the handler divides by it to compute `pages`, so omitting it or sending 0 causes a server error.

parameters.name: pageNum
parameters.description: 1-based page number. Values < 1 are treated as 1; non-numeric is treated as 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Items per page. Effectively required (>= 1): a missing/zero value causes a divide-by-zero in the handler. No upper bound is enforced.

parameters.name: roleVisibility
parameters.description: Filter by visibility. `public` also matches `waitReview` cards. Empty = all.

parameters.name: creationMethod
parameters.description: Filter by the stored creation method (e.g. `hearthroom`, `open_api`, `mcp`, `manual`, `ai_summarize`, `import`, `clone`). Not validated against a whitelist: an unknown value simply yields an empty list. Cards created via `POST /role` store the whitelisted `origin` if given, otherwise `open_api`.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Viewer language used for text conversion of list items.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Platform scope. Cards with `from` equal to this value or `all` are listed. Clients normally omit it.

400.description: Database error; body `{"error": "<raw error string>"}`.

403.description: `service_account_forbidden`.

get.summary: Get the published custom preview page of a role
get.description: Returns the author-designed preview page document for a role, as seen by viewers. Guest-readable. The document is only served when the role is publicly visible (`roleVisibility` is `public` or `waitReview`) and a preview page exists with status pending (1) or passed (2); in every other case (private role, unknown role, no page, rejected page, serving kill switch active, or a load error) the response is still 200 with `{"doc": null, "version": 0}`. The `doc` is an opaque JSON document produced by the preview-page editor; its internal structure is not part of this contract. When the visual kill switch is active, `skinId` is returned empty and decorative properties are stripped from `doc`.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Role id.

400.description: `invalid_param` — `roleId` missing. Body is `{"error": "invalid_param"}`.

401.description: `unauthorized` — an Authorization header was sent but is invalid.

get.summary: Validate an owned role and report limits
get.description: Runs the pre-publish validation on a card owned by the bearer and returns blockers (missing `roleName`/`roleWelcome`/`roleDetailDesc`, fields over their character limit, HTML/XMLV3 markup problems in the opening), warnings (missing avatar/background, quality heuristics), suggested fixes, quality dimensions and a token-budget report whose `limits` block lists the hard per-field character limits for this card's language. Clients should read limits from here rather than hard-coding them. `status` is `blocker` when any blocker exists, `warning` when only warnings exist, else `pass`.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Role id.

400.description: `roleId is required`.

403.description: `permission_denied`.

500.description: `record not found` or another unclassified error; `retryable: true`.

patch.summary: Patch profile fields and/or the definition of an owned private role
patch.description: Updates a subset of fields on a card owned by the bearer. Fields are pointers: a key that is absent is not touched. The role must be `private` (public/waitReview cards reject with `public_role_requires_clone`; use `POST /role/{roleId}/visibility` first). Profile block (`roleName`, `roleDesc`, `roleTag`, `userName`) and definition block (`roleDetailDesc`) are applied as two sequential writes; if the second fails after the first succeeded the profile change persists. Caveats of the profile block: an empty-string `roleName`/`roleDesc`/`userName` and an empty `roleTag` array are ignored (nothing is cleared) — to clear a field use `POST /role/{roleId}/document`. `roleDesc` is limited to the language budget (500 chars, 2500 for English cards). `roleDetailDesc` replaces the whole definition; an empty/blank value is rejected (`empty_field_patch`); limit 10000 chars (50000 for English cards). At least one key must be present or the request fails with `nothing to update`. Length-limit violations (`role_desc_too_long`, `role_detail_too_long`) and `public_role_requires_clone`/`empty_field_patch` are surfaced as HTTP 500 by the error mapper (their codes do not match the 400 substrings), with `retryable: true`. A missing role surfaces as 500 `record not found`.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Role id. Only the path parameter is honoured.

200.description: Updated role summary (result of the last applied block).

400.description: `invalid JSON body`, `nothing to update` (body `{"error": "..."}`).

403.description: `permission_denied` — not the author.

500.description: `record not found`, `public_role_requires_clone`, `role_desc_too_long`, `role_detail_too_long`, `empty_field_patch`, or another unclassified error; `{"error": "<code>", "retryable": true}`.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a role card owned by the bearer, cascading to follows, search/tag indexes, worldbook bindings, conversations and memories. Not reversible. Ownership is checked before the cascade.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Role id.

403.description: `permission_denied: not the author of this role`.

put.summary: Replace the display rules of an owned role
put.description: Full replacement of the author asset (there is no partial update). Optimistic locking: `version` must equal the version last read (`0` when no asset exists yet); a mismatch returns 409 `version_conflict`. `mountLayer` is required and must be `under`, `over` or `cover`; `pageMode` may be omitted (treated as `classic`) or `immersive`. Every rule needs a non-blank `find`; each `replace` is limited to 131072 bytes and the sum of `id`+`name`+`find`+`replace` across all rules to 33554432 bytes (`validate_reject`, with `message` and `detail` `{reason: emptyFind|ruleReplace|rulesTotal, index, name, max, actual, unit: bytes}`). Saving sets `status` to `passed` immediately and increments `version`. Rules act on the rendering layer only and never enter the prompt.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Role id owned by the caller.

400.description: `invalid_param` (bad JSON) or `validate_reject` (unknown mountLayer/pageMode, empty `find`, rule or total size over limit). Body `{"error": "<code>"}`; for empty `find` and size limits also `message` (English sentence) and `detail` `{reason, index (0-based, -1 for the whole set), name, max, actual, unit: "bytes"}`.

403.description: `forbidden` — not the role owner.

409.description: `version_conflict` — `version` does not match the stored version (also when an asset already exists and `version` is 0).

delete.summary: Remove the display rules of an owned role
delete.description: Deletes the author asset so the role renders without display rules. Idempotent: succeeds when no asset exists.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Role id owned by the caller.

post.summary: Write many role fields in one request
post.description: Applies a partial document to an owned private role in a single write. Every key under `fields` is optional; absent keys are untouched, present keys overwrite (an empty string clears the field where allowed). `fieldPatches` carries anchored text edits (`operations`) applied on top of the current value of the corresponding field and is the way to edit long text without resending it. At least one key under `fields` must be present (`nothing to update` otherwise); if nothing is effectively changed (e.g. only a blank `roleName`), the service answers `invalid_arguments`. Rules: `roleName` blank is ignored; `roleAvatar`/`roleBackground` blank is ignored, otherwise must be an http(s) URL (`invalid_asset_url`); `roleSex` accepts `man|women|other` and aliases (`male`, `female`, `woman`, `男`, `女`, `其他`; empty clears; else `invalid_role_sex`); `talkExample[].roleType` accepts `ai|user` (`assistant` maps to `ai`) and `content` must be non-blank (`invalid_talk_example`); `roleTag` replaces the whole tag list (each non-blank string becomes a platform tag `{icon:"", text, type:2}`); `jailbreak` is writable here but is never returned by v1 read routes. Character limits depend on the card language (see `GET /role/validate` → `tokenBudget.limits`): roleDesc 500 (English 2500), roleDetailDesc 10000 (English 50000), roleWelcome 8000 (English 10000), jailbreak 500 for zh-Hant/zh-Hans, 1500 otherwise, roleOutputContract 2000. Violations return `<field>_too_long` codes (`role_desc_too_long`, `role_detail_too_long`, `role_welcome_too_long`, `jailbreak_too_long`, `role_output_contract_too_long`), which the error mapper surfaces as HTTP 500 with `retryable: true`. The role must be `private` (`public_role_requires_clone`). Alternates/prologue greetings are not part of this document — use `PATCH /role/{roleId}/welcome`.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Role id. Only the path parameter is honoured; a `roleId` inside the body is ignored.

400.description: `invalid JSON body`, `nothing to update` (body `{"error": "..."}`), or `invalid_arguments` (nothing effectively patched; `{"error","retryable":false}`).

403.description: `permission_denied`.

post.summary: Submit an owned private role for publication review
post.description: Submits the card to moderation. Requires an explicit confirmation: `userConfirmed` must be `true` and `confirmationSummary` must be at least 8 characters (`confirmation_required`). The role must be `private` (`publish_requires_private_role`) and must have non-empty `roleName`, `roleWelcome`, `roleDetailDesc`, `roleAvatar` and `roleBackground` (`validation_blocker`). On success an asynchronous moderation task starts and the response carries `reviewStatus: "running"` with its `taskId`; the card becomes `public` (reviewStatus `passed`), goes to human review (`waitReview`/`pending`), or is returned to `private` with `suggest_r18`/`rejected` when the task completes. If the card is already in the human-review queue or is flagged for forced human review, no task is created and `reviewStatus` is `pending` without `taskId`. Poll `GET /role/detail` (`roleVisibility`, `reviewStatus`, `reviewReason`) for the outcome.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Role id.

400.description: `invalid JSON body`; `confirmation_required`; `validation_blocker` (required content or assets missing).

403.description: `permission_denied`.

404.description: `role_not_found` (role vanished between ownership check and submission).

500.description: `record not found`, `publish_requires_private_role`, or another unclassified error; `retryable: true`.
