put.summary: Create or update a trial card from a local file
put.description: Upserts an auto-expiring private role card identified by the client's own key (typically a local draft id). First call creates a private role (idempotency key `trial:<clientKey>`), registers it as a trial card and applies the payload; later calls re-apply only the sections whose content hash changed (`sections` in the response holds the stored hashes). Sections: `card` (role fields, same shape as `POST /role/{roleId}/document` `fields`; `card.roleName` is overwritten by top-level `name` and `card.roleWelcome` is dropped — openings live in `welcome`), `welcome`, `worldbook` and `authorAsset`. `welcome`, `worldbook` and `authorAsset` are whole-document sections: omitting one that was previously stored clears it (welcome reset, worldbook deleted, display rules reset); omitting `card` leaves the card as is. Worldbook entries are diffed by content hash: unchanged entries are kept, new ones created, missing ones deleted; entries with `isEnabled:false` and exact duplicates are ignored. Limits: request body 48 MiB; `name` <= 100 chars and required on create; <= 1000 worldbook entries, each `content` <= 3000 chars and non-blank when enabled; display rule `replace` <= 131072 bytes, all rules <= 33554432 bytes, `find` non-blank; role field limits as for `/role/{roleId}/document`. Slots: when the account already has `slots.max` active trial cards, creation fails with 409 `trial_slots_full` naming the least recently active card; send `evict: true` to purge that card and proceed. Every successful PUT refreshes `expiresAt` to now + TTL; a background sweep purges expired cards (role, conversations, worldbook and rules) unless they were played recently, in which case expiry is extended from the last play. Trial cards do not appear in `GET /role/mine`. When the worldbook service is unavailable and the payload contains `worldbook`, nothing is written (503). Note: clearing a previously stored `welcome` by omitting it sends an empty opening to the role service, which rejects blank openings (`empty_field_patch`, surfaced as HTTP 500); to remove an opening send a new non-blank one instead.

bearerResolution: The identity middleware on the /open/v1 group reads only `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Raw `accountId`, `accountToken` and test-account headers sent by the client are deleted/overwritten and never trusted.

Resolution order for a non-empty bearer: (1) if it starts with `lsk_` it is treated as a service-account key and looked up by SHA-256 hash; a revoked/unknown key, a non-service account or a banned account yields 401 `unauthorized` (no fall-through). (2) Otherwise it is tried as an OAuth access token; it must be unexpired, unrevoked and bound (token and session) to the resource `<API_BASE>/open/v1`; an MCP-resource token is rejected here. (3) Otherwise it is tried as a legacy first-party account token (official web/app login state). Anything else is 401 `unauthorized`.
A bearer that is present but invalid is always 401, even on guest-readable routes; only a completely absent Authorization header is downgraded to guest.
Service-account keys are additionally restricted to an allow-list; a valid key on any other route is 403 `service_account_forbidden` from the middleware (the handler is never reached).
For OAuth bearers the middleware also records the OAuth `client_id` that issued the token; role-share grants created through such a token store that client id.

The middleware sets request defaults `from=app` and `X-Client-Platform=web` when the client did not send them (web clients are not subject to app-store content filtering). The optional `language` header (`zh-Hant`, `zh-Hans`, `en`, `ja`, `ko`) selects localized strings and, for comments, the locale filter.
x-auth-notes.guestNote: Guest routes are matched on the gin route pattern (not the raw path). On a guest request the identity is empty; comment handlers then return `isLiked`/`isOwner`/`canDelete` = false and hide the caller's own rejected comments. If a valid bearer is sent it is used normally.
x-auth-notes.serviceKeyFormat: `lsk_` followed by 43 base64url characters (32 random bytes). The key is shown once at creation; only its first 12 characters (`keyPrefix`) are retrievable afterwards.
